profiles.def-hh-cell-datum-dominance-and-cell-ide: The cell-datum carrier defines a finite basis with a coefficient axiom and then verifies dominance, two-sided higher spans and a quotient basis. Its Definition gives data and its Verification proves consequences; it does not assert a predicate equivalence requiring a converse theorem.
profiles.lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-: This carrier constructs the unique generator-fixing reversal on a quotient and checks preservation of every defining relation. Existence, uniqueness and the finite restriction are direct assertions, not an equivalence between two hypotheses.
profiles.def-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-elements: The Murphy carrier specifies the cyclotomic polynomial factor and row symmetrizer, verifies their commutation and computes the swapped-index involution. It defines elements before asserting any basis property, so no iff implication is being withheld.
profiles.lem-hh-type-a-garnir-straightening-and-m: The ordinary theorem asserts an integral basis, dominance ideals and an independent-first-index multiplication congruence. The trace/sign argument proves these assertions directly; neither semisimplicity nor another condition is stated to be equivalent to them.
profiles.lem-hh-componentwise-initial-row-straigh: The componentwise theorem gives a supported expansion and a finite-generator congruence. Coset factorization and initial-segment counting establish these conclusions; no necessary-and-sufficient characterization occurs in its Statement.
profiles.lem-hh-cyclotomic-component-shift-and-do: The shift carrier states a polynomial transport identity and its ideal consequences. Its first summand and strictly dominating second summand are proved from that identity; there is no converse condition equivalent to a premise.
profiles.thm-hh-cyclotomic-murphy-basis-and-cellu: Cyclotomic cellularity asserts a universal basis and cell multiplication identities, followed by arbitrary commutative base change. The final square spanning matrix proves existence of that basis; the Statement is not a semisimplicity criterion or other iff claim.
profiles.thm-hh-cell-modules-forms-and-radicals: The form carrier constructs coefficient modules, their unique invariant product form and a stable radical over an arbitrary commutative ring. These are direct construction properties, not a biconditional characterizing when a form is nondegenerate.
profiles.thm-hh-cellular-simple-module-classifica: The classification has two actual directions: nonzero form heads are absolutely simple, and each simple module is obtained as one such head. Both directions are checked below using the rank-one action and maximal-first cell filtration rather than being dismissed as absent.
profiles.ex-hh-rank-one-cyclotomic-cell-modules-a: The level-two rank-one example directly computes the two form scalars and the collision algebra of dual numbers. It does not characterize all parameter values by an iff assertion; its repeated-root calculation is a stated case.
profiles.ex-hh-type-a-rank-two-cell-module-specia: The rank-two ordinary example computes the row Murphy form and its vanishing at the negative unit parameter, and separately states the signed-conjugate convention. No converse parameter classification is claimed.
profiles.lem-hh-type-a-murphy-strong-tableau-stra: Strong ordinary straightening asserts zero coefficients outside two prefix upper sets and a sorted-composition shape bound. The finite incidence inverse and integral coordinate injection prove a support assertion, not an equivalence between unrelated hypotheses.
profiles.lem-hh-finite-direct-summands-over-khh-a: This lemma starts with an idempotent projection and constructs a free basis of its image, with rank read from reduction. The Nakayama-style finite matrix argument and separatedness prove a one-way conclusion; no converse characterization is stated.
profiles.lem-hh-idempotents-lift-over-formal-powe: The idempotent lemma lifts a specified finite complete orthogonal family by a Newton limit and finite corner induction. It is an existence assertion with fixed reduction, not a biconditional about arbitrary families.
profiles.lem-hh-formal-deformation-matrix-unit-li: The matrix-unit theorem assumes a specified split residue algebra, lifts its diagonal idempotents and constructs an exact matrix-unit basis. Its Statement asserts an isomorphism reducing to the given one, with no separate converse predicate.
profiles.lem-hh-type-a-quantum-antipode-descends: Antipode descent is proved by checking all relators and both convolution identities on generators, then words. The Statement asserts these two Hopf identities, not a biconditional; left and right convolution obligations are both already proved in steps 4.1 and 5.1.
profiles.ex-hh-ariki-koike-rank-one-level-two-quo: This example expands a fixed monic quadratic and supplies its two-element basis and polynomial inverse. It states these calculations directly, without a necessary-and-sufficient condition on the parameters.
profiles.ex-hh-ariki-koike-rank-two-level-two-pbw: The eight-word example explicitly enumerates four exponent pairs and two symmetric-group words, then applies the PBW basis theorem. It is a fixed rank/level calculation, not an equivalence claim.
profiles.ex-hh-ariki-koike-colliding-content-spec: The collision example fixes the map sending both root parameters to one and shows the interpolation denominator vanishes there. It does not assert that every failure of a projector is equivalent to this particular collision.

endpoint_reviews.def-hh-specialization-and-regular-trace-: Regular-trace specialization is parametrized by ring homomorphisms to fields and changes of finite bases, not an ordered interval. The Definition and Remarks compare a determinant with its coefficient image and a square basis-change factor; no endpoint limit is asserted.
endpoint_reviews.lem-hh-one-parameter-formal-series-local: The topology is formal h-adic: step 1.3 constructs eventual coefficients at every finite precision and proves their intersection is zero. There is no interval of numerical h-values or limiting endpoint requiring a separate one-sided assertion.
endpoint_reviews.lem-hh-finite-direct-summands-over-khh-a: The projection rank is a nonnegative integer, and its zero value is explicitly treated in step 3.1 and the empty basis in step 5.1. The present endpoint row concerns no additional interval or limit parameter beyond those zero-rank cases.
endpoint_reviews.lem-hh-idempotents-lift-over-formal-powe: Newton corrections are indexed by all nonnegative iteration numbers and square the error order; they do not approach an endpoint in an ordered parameter interval. Step 4.1 separately proves the empty and singleton-family induction starts.
endpoint_reviews.lem-hh-regular-trace-criterion-in-charac: The trace criterion is an implication for a finite-dimensional field algebra, proved by nilpotence of its radical and a finite maximal-ideal descent. Its Statement ranges over fields without an interval or endpoint parameter; no characteristic endpoint limit is used.
endpoint_reviews.lem-hh-formal-deformation-matrix-unit-li: This formal lifting result compares one residue algebra with its complete formal deformation. Step 1.1 handles no blocks and the remaining proof lifts finitely many matrix corners; there is no ordered parameter range with an endpoint assertion.
endpoint_reviews.thm-hh-generic-finite-hecke-semisimplici: The generic Hecke result tests whether a Laurent determinant vanishes under a field homomorphism. The all-one specialization certifies a nonzero polynomial, not an endpoint of a numerical parameter interval; the trivial group is handled in step 5.1.
endpoint_reviews.thm-hh-split-deformation-labels-and-exce: The label theorem distinguishes a formal residue fiber from a fraction-field fiber and separately makes a determinant-nonvanishing implication. It explicitly declines to identify the exceptional zero set with the nonsimple locus, so no interval boundary classification is suppressed.
endpoint_reviews.cex-hh-nondegenerate-symmetrizing-trace-: The counterexample fixes the complex parameter to the imaginary unit and calculates a square-zero nonzero element plus two Gram matrices. There is no varying ordered parameter interval; the failure is exhibited at one fixed algebra.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-two-dimensional-formal-split-defor: In the formal rank-two example, one plus h is a unit because its constant coefficient is one; its inverse is an alternating coefficient sequence in step 2.1. Formal h is not evaluated along an interval or at a singular numerical endpoint.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-ariki-koike-level-one-is-finite-ty: The level-one example has positive integral rank and unit Laurent parameters, and its map sends a finite basis to a finite basis. There is no numerical interval or limiting endpoint; the singleton rank is a generator-free instance of the same presentation.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-ariki-koike-rank-one-level-two-quo: The quotient example fixes rank one and level two and allows arbitrary unit field elements as roots. The monic division and inverse identity have no parameter interval or endpoint convention; coincident roots are permitted without an endpoint limit.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-ariki-koike-rank-two-level-two-pbw: The PBW example fixes both rank and level at two. Its finite exponent set is explicitly enumerated in step 1.2; this does not leave an interval parameter or a limiting endpoint to interpret.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-ariki-koike-colliding-content-spec: The content-collision example specifies one algebraic specialization into the rationals, rather than a family indexed by an ordered interval. The undefined denominator is a zero-specialization issue already calculated in step 2.1, not an omitted endpoint limit.
endpoint_reviews.lem-hh-cyclotomic-anti-involution-fixes-: Reversal preserves each valid defining relation for the stated generator ranges. At rank one the finite-generator relations disappear, already covered by the empty and singleton cases; there is no independent interval endpoint assertion about reversal.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-rank-one-cyclotomic-cell-modules-a: The rank-one cell example fixes two root parameters in a field and treats their coincidence algebraically. It neither orders these roots nor takes a limit through an interval; the collision form is computed at the exact equal-root specialization.
endpoint_reviews.ex-hh-type-a-rank-two-cell-module-specia: This example computes the specialized algebra at the negative unit value exactly, without approaching it along an ordered interval. The boundary obligation is form degeneration, which its square-zero calculation handles, not an endpoint convention.

lem-hh-rank-one-cyclotomic-quotient-moni.empty: The detector sees the cyclotomic product, but its index runs from one to the positive level r stipulated by the defining presentation.
